Alger, 16 août 2026 (Algeria Tech) — Ant: Algiers, August 16, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — Anthropic announced the integration of an invisible watermark in every text produced by its Claude AI models since August 2, a transparency measure mandated by the European AI Act. The company justifies this choice using a method validated by Google DeepMind, while acknowledging the limitations of this approach.
Une réponse aux obligations de transpare: A response to the transparency obligations of the AI Act
Depuis le 2 août, les fournisseurs d’IA: Since August 2, AI providers must guarantee the identifiability of generated content, under penalty of fines of up to 15 million euros or 3% of global turnover. Anthropic has opted for a radical technical solution: an invisible watermark integrated directly into every text produced by its Claude models, deployed globally. This initiative has triggered mixed reactions, ranging from tracking concerns to questions about the quality of the generated texts.
Le 14 août, Anthropic a publié un billet: On August 14, Anthropic published a detailed post to address criticisms and clarify how this method works. Named SynthID-Text, the technology is inspired by a solution developed by Google DeepMind and validated in the journal Nature in late 2024. It relies on a sequence derived from a secret key, replacing the randomness inherent in word choice with an identifiable pattern. Anthropic compares this process to a game of Monopoly where the dice are replaced by the decimals of pi: unpredictable for users, but traceable by those who know the key.
Des limites techniques et des angles mor: Recognized technical limitations and blind spots
La cartographie des usages révèle des di: The mapping of use cases reveals disparities in the effectiveness of the watermark. Translations, where every word is generated by the model, are systematically watermarked. Conversely, light proofreading or minor modifications of human-generated texts leave little or no trace due to insufficient rewriting. Code, on the other hand, is difficult to watermark, as syntactic constraints limit plausible alternatives.
Anthropic admet que le filigrane n’est p: Anthropic admits that the watermark is not foolproof. A short text, heavy rewriting, or mixing with human prose can dilute the signal, making detection uncertain. The mark only identifies that text passed through a Claude model, without ever tracing back to an account or an individual. The company also acknowledges the impossibility of restricting the mechanism to Europe due to the lack of a reliable control mechanism.
Retour sur les précédents échecs des dét: Looking back at previous failures of AI text detectors
La fiabilité des filigranes contraste av: The reliability of watermarks contrasts with the setbacks faced by AI text detectors. OpenAI launched its own tool in January 2023, before withdrawing it six months later due to an unacceptable error rate: 26% correct detection of AI-generated text, with 9% false positives. GPTZero and Pangram, two commercial players in the sector, regularly battle over studies regarding their false positive rates, a problem compounded for non-native English speakers.
Anthropic souligne d’ailleurs que son pr: Anthropic also points out that its own model exhibits recurring stylistic tics, such as the construction "it's not X, it's Y." However, the SynthID-Text solution stands out for its proactive approach: unlike detectors that analyze texts a posteriori, the watermark is applied at the source. Google DeepMind claims that its method did not degrade user satisfaction during tests on nearly 20 million responses generated by Gemini, although this figure comes from the technology's creator.
Une API de détection promise pour évalue: A detection API promised to evaluate effectiveness
Pour répondre aux interrogations, Anthro: To address questions, Anthropic has announced the upcoming deployment of an API to test watermark detection on generated texts. In the meantime, users should know that their texts entrusted to Claude will carry an invisible mark, without their explicit consent. This transparency raises ethical and technical questions, as the debate on the traceability of AI-generated content remains open.
